tools.name: Stanford sycophancy study
tools.detail: Quoted: models endorsed the user 49% more often than humans; endorsed problematic behavior 47% of the time

claims: Stanford study: Claude/AI agrees with you 49% more than a human would; models endorse harmful/problematic behavior 47% of the time
Karpathy 'recently left to work for Anthropic' (as stated by creator)

/llm-council spawns 5 advisors: contrarian (what fails), first-principles (rips assumptions), expansionist (upside missed), outsider (knows nothing of your industry), executor (what you do Monday morning)
Each advisor blind-reviews the others' answers; a chairman agent gives the final call and next steps
The faithful version spawns different providers (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, xAI) rather than Claude subagents
how_to_steps: Install the creator's skill (comment 'council') or build from Karpathy's repo
Type /llm-council followed by the decision question
Advisors blind-review each other's answers (no author labels)
Chairman agent synthesizes a verdict + 'Do this next'
Optionally run the faithful cross-vendor mode via OpenRouter-style providers
